about: Listener verdicts, by ear, on engine builds, and the pairs they order; each build's reasons are tags (synthetic, clean, slow-attack, breathy-attack, janky, reference, liked). Any distance must rank these pairs right (python -m awvafit backtest) before it enters an objective. The renders are not here: $AWVA_VERDICTS/<set>/<instrument>__<build>.mono.f32 (48 kHz mono float32) with <set>/<instrument>.notes.json (the schedule: note, dyn, t_on, t_off in the key stream's time; the audio starts at the first note's t_on).

trumpet/iter1.label: the physical trumpet, Track B iteration 1 (the brass family v3's trumpet preset, bit for bit)

trumpet/hybrid.label: the brass engine's trumpet preset (the approved reference)

sets.main: 4 pitches x 3 dynamics, 1.6 s sustained notes: strike / pressure 0.2 / 0.12 (pp), 0.45 / 0.4 (mf), 0.75 / 0.85 (ff)
sets.soft: soft strikes, as the recorded takes play: 4 pitches x strikes 0.07, 0.12, 0.2, 0.3 at pressure 0.4 (stimuli.strike_set)

attack.why: decisive at soft strikes; at medium and hard strikes against recordings it prefers the rejected old trumpet

jtfs.why: the best timbre ranker against real recordings; small margins on stage 2

mrstft.why: right on the old-trumpet pairs, blind to stage 2

noise.why: per dynamic, gated on the recording's noise floor; reported, not scored

lanes.why: the lanes' objective terms against recordings prefer the rejected old trumpet
